Connection status

What this box does

Caspian uses a config you already have to connect to a server. It shares that one connection as a WiFi network. Every device that joins leaves through the same tunnel, and you install nothing on the device itself.

The dot above the box is where names are looked up. DNS requests from your devices come to this box and are answered from inside the tunnel, not from the network the box itself sits on.

Two ways to wire it

Caspian needs two things: a way to reach the internet, and an adapter to make the hotspot with. You choose which adapter does which job.

Arrangement one: internet over the cable

The simplest arrangement, and the one to use if you have a cable. The internet arrives on the cable and the built-in WiFi becomes the hotspot. While Caspian is on, the built-in WiFi is no longer joined to your home network, because one adapter cannot do both jobs at once.

Arrangement two: internet over WiFi

For places with no cable. Plug in a USB WiFi adapter, take the internet from one of the two adapters and build the hotspot on the other. Either can play either role, and you choose in advanced settings.

You do not need to unplug anything. If both a cable and WiFi are connected, choose which one reaches the internet in advanced settings. Caspian uses the one you choose, as long as it really has internet on it.

Why there are two controls

Two controls on the dashboard can stop the internet for your devices. They stop different things. Read this before you press one in a hurry.

The switch: on and off

The switch turns the whole box on and off. Off stops the tunnel. Off also stops the WiFi hotspot and the address and name service on it. If Caspian unblocked the radio, off blocks it again. The WiFi network that your devices joined stops existing, and every one of them disconnects. Caspian also undoes each network change it made, so the box goes back to how Caspian found it.

Client traffic: cut and resume

This control stops only the traffic that Caspian forwards for your devices. Nothing else stops. The tunnel stays up. The hotspot stays up, your devices keep their addresses, and they stay joined. This page stays open on a joined device, because the panel is traffic to this box and not traffic through it. Press Resume client traffic, and your devices reach the internet again.

If you hold only a phone that is on the Caspian WiFi, and you switch the box off, the WiFi goes with it. The phone leaves the network and cannot open this page again. By default this page is open only on the hotspot address. Opening it from the local network stays off until you switch it on in advanced settings. The client traffic control does not have this hazard. The WiFi stays up, so the phone stays joined, opens this page, and puts the traffic back.

When you want the traffic to stop now, and you want to put it back yourself, press the client traffic control. It is the emergency stop. It works at once, it asks for no confirmation, and your devices do not have to join the WiFi again afterwards. When you have finished with the box, or you want the WiFi adapter back on your own network, press the switch. Do not use the switch as an emergency stop from a phone on the hotspot.

A cut is held in memory only and is written to no file, so a restart of the box removes it. Caspian does not switch itself on after a restart, so press the switch to start it again. Client traffic then flows.

What each control does

Switch on
Switches the whole box on and off: the tunnel and the hotspot together. Switching off also takes the WiFi down, so every joined device is disconnected.
Cut client traffic
Stops client traffic at once while leaving the hotspot up. Devices stay joined and can still open this page, but nothing reaches the internet. Restarting the box clears this state, but Caspian comes back switched off, so traffic does not return until you press the switch.
Your config
The link your provider gave you. Caspian stores it, never shows it back to you and never writes it into any log. To use a different server, paste a new link over it.
Your WiFi
The name and password of the network this box broadcasts. The password is at least 8 characters. Changing either disconnects the devices that are joined, and they have to join again.
Which connection reaches the internet
Which adapter brings the internet in. Leave it empty and Caspian chooses. If you choose, that adapter has to have internet on it at that moment, or Caspian refuses to start and says why.
Which adapter makes the hotspot
Which adapter makes the hotspot. It has to be a WiFi adapter, and it cannot be the same one that brings the internet in.
Channel
The radio channel of the hotspot. If the internet and the hotspot are on the same adapter, the channel is pinned to whatever network that adapter is joined to and cannot be chosen.
Country
The two-letter country code. It decides which channels and what power are allowed. A wrong code can stop the hotspot from coming up at all.
Hotspot network
The range of addresses handed to joined devices. Change it only if it clashes with a network you already use.
Also open this panel from the network this box is attached to
Lets this page be opened from the network the box sits on, not only from the hotspot. It is off by default.

What is protected, and what is not

What this box really does

  • If the tunnel drops, traffic from your devices stops rather than leaving by another route. This rule does not need the tunnel to exist. It names only the hotspot and the internet connection, so a tunnel that disappears cannot loosen it.
  • Caspian redirects DNS requests from your devices to this box and answers them from inside the tunnel. DNS over TLS is rejected and DNS over QUIC is dropped, so a device cannot step around that path.
  • While Caspian is on, the box itself cannot reach the internet directly except for a few named things: getting an address, setting its clock, looking up names, and reaching your server. So you cannot update this box's software until you switch Caspian off.
  • Devices joined to the hotspot cannot see each other. On this box they reach nothing except the services it offers them.
  • Your config is never shown back on screen and never written into any log. The server address is stripped even from error text.
  • If Caspian takes your WiFi adapter for the hotspot, it records every change it makes and reverses each one on the way out, so the box rejoins your own network.

What this box does not do

This list is not shortened to be reassuring. If you are relying on this box, these are the things to know.

  • DNS over HTTPS, on port 443, looks the same as ordinary HTTPS. Such a request goes through the tunnel, so it is not a leak. This box cannot see it, and can promise nothing about it.
  • IPv6 for your devices is always blocked. This is not a setting: this version refuses every other value, because a device with a working IPv6 path prefers it over IPv4 and would go around the tunnel.
  • The guarantee covers the traffic Caspian forwards for your devices. The box's own traffic is outside it, because the connection software has to reach your server over the internet, or there is no tunnel at all.
  • This box does not protect your devices from themselves. If an app on your phone gives you away, the tunnel carries that just as faithfully.
  • The hotspot is protected with WPA2. Anybody with the WiFi password can join, so treat it as a key.

When something is not working

I cannot see the WiFi name
First check that the top of this page says connected. If it says something else, the hotspot did not come up and the reason is in that message. If it is connected and you still see nothing, look at the channel and the country code in advanced settings. A wrong country code can silence the radio.
I am joined but there is no internet
When the tunnel drops, this is what you see, and it is deliberate: Caspian stops the traffic instead of letting it out another way. Look at the top of the page. If it says traffic is cut, somebody pressed the cut control, and the button next to it puts the traffic back.
It is slow
All traffic goes through one connection and one server, so the speed depends on that server and how far you are from it. If you have more than one config, try another one. A config change takes a few seconds.
I cannot reach this page
Open it from a device joined to the hotspot. While Caspian is on, this page is always reachable that way, even while traffic is cut. Reaching it from the network the box itself sits on is off by default and is turned on in advanced settings.
I have forgotten the password for this page
Recovering a forgotten password requires access to the device itself. On a Mac, open the Caspian app and choose Reset Password. On other devices, use the installer's local password recovery tool. If you still know your password, sign in and change it in the panel's password section.
